summary: Mrs. Mizrachi examines the historical experiences of Jewish communities in medieval Spain and the Muslim world, contrasting their integration and intellectual contributions with the conditions of Jews in Christian Europe. She discusses the lives and perspectives of figures like Hasday Ibn Shaprut, Yehuda Halevi, and Rambam to illustrate how these scholars navigated their environments while maintaining their commitment to Torah. The class emphasizes shifting the narrative of Jewish history away from victimhood toward a perspective of strength, resilience, and active engagement with the world.
questions: How did the status of Jews in the Muslim world differ from those in Christian Europe during the medieval period?
What was the role of Jewish intellectuals in the caliphate of Spain?
How did Yehuda Halevi view the relationship between philosophy and Torah?
Why does Mrs. Mizrachi argue against the narrative of Jewish victimhood in history?
How did the experience of Rambam in Spain and North Africa shape his approach to Jewish survival?
